Expense changes with the comparator, reliability varies by task, and successful benchmark defenses qualify the security generalization. Prices also cannot establish profit. The retrieved evidence supports concerns without establishing the whole claim.
limitations: Several findings are company demonstrations or unreviewed preprints.
Benchmark results do not directly measure the entire deployed agent population.
The exact experiment dates for the compiler example are unavailable.
The financial wording is insufficiently specified for an accounting verdict.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLM-based agents, which Anthropic profits from, are expensive to run, unreliable and extremely difficult to secure.

statement.excerpt: And then there are the endless negative externalities of LLMs, which Anthropic regularly profits from; the latest is agents, expensive to run, unreliable and extremely difficult to secure.
statement.document_title: There are no heroes in commercial AI

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading concerns commercially offered LLM agents performing multistep tasks, including Claude-based agents.

Expense means substantial operating costs relative to simpler workflows; reliability means dependable task completion without frequent correction; security concerns include malicious instructions encountered through tools.
No universal failure rate, cost threshold or security guarantee is implied.
The ongoing state is assessed for February 2026, the latest completed month before the post. This reporting window is an evaluator choice.
“Profits from” ordinarily means commercial benefit here. It does not clearly specify revenue, gross profit or net income, so the monetary component has an unknown accounting basis.
criteria.support_condition: Representative evidence establishes substantial operating costs, material reliability limitations and persistent security difficulties in the target period, alongside substantiated commercial benefit to Anthropic.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evidence refutes one or more asserted characteristics across the relevant agent uses. Isolated successes or inexpensive tasks do not by themselves refute a broad tendency.

evidence.excerpt: Pricing remains the same at $5/$25 per million tokens
evidence.locator: Launch overview, availability and pricing paragraph
evidence.explanation: The launch establishes a paid model offered for agentic work. Token prices establish neither representative task costs nor Anthropic's realized revenue or profit.

evidence.excerpt: still lags behind the most skilled humans
evidence.explanation: Anthropic acknowledges remaining computer-use limitations while reporting substantial improvements. Relative performance below skilled humans does not by itself establish that agents generally fail a reasonable reliability standard.

evidence.excerpt: a fraction of what it would cost me
evidence.explanation: The compiler experiment reports nearly $20,000 in API costs, yet its author considers that cheap relative to equivalent personal work. The experiment spans two weeks without precise dates, so it is contextual rather than a February-only measurement.

AgentDyn reports that tested defenses either left security weaknesses or impaired legitimate task completion. This supports the security-difficulty component for its tested workflows, not every agent deployment.

AgentSentry reports no successful attacks in its evaluated benchmark and preserved task utility. This qualifies a blanket security pessimism, but a bounded benchmark does not demonstrate robust security against all adaptive attacks.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Representative February 2026 task-level cost and repeated-success measurements, realistic security evaluations across common agent configurations, and a defined, documented measure of Anthropic's commercial benefit.
